citeinfo.title: United States Documented Orphaned Well Database 2026
citeinfo.othercit: Update to: Grove, C.A., and Merrill, M.D., 2022, United States Documented Unplugged Orphaned Oil and Gas Well Dataset: U.S. Geological Survey data release, https://doi.org/10.5066/P91PJETI

descript.abstract: The United States Documented Orphaned Well Database (DOWDB) contains 130,121 unplugged oil and gas wells in 28 states. This release of the data is an update to, and supersedes, the initial version (Grove and Merrill, 2022). The definition of an orphaned oil or gas well varies across data sources; the database includes oil or gas wells where the state indicates that the well is an unplugged orphan, or the following criteria are met: 1) no production for 6 to 24 months depending on the state (an average of 12 months), 2) the well is unplugged, 3) there is no responsible party to manage the well for future re-use or for plugging and abandonment, and 4) the location of the well is documented. The database includes location coordinates, American Petroleum Institute (API) number, or other identification number, well type, well status, and additional information for each unplugged orphaned well. In this update, completely new orphaned wells records were obtained from the states. As an additional feature, the authors estimated surface and subsurface rights ownership using maps of land ownership, and have attributed that information to the well records. Ownership information here is not official; it is a product of spatial operations that do not account for location errors or actual lease details. Ownership information at the well level was not provided by the states or Bureau of Land Management. Please confirm well responsibility with the appropriate agency or office. All other data were collected from the respective state agency overseeing oil and gas wells via online data sources or by direct requests. Location format conversion was performed on wells without coordinate locations using tools provided by the Bureau of Land Management and some state agencies. No other data manipulations were performed to the source data aside from reformatting or the addition of explanatory notes.
descript.purpose: The database was created to provide documented orphaned well data to decision makers, as well as researchers, and other interested parties in a publicly available online format.
descript.supplinf: The file contains data available in comma separated value (.csv) file format. The user must have software capable of opening and viewing a .csv file. Opening the csv formatted file in certain spreadsheet viewing/editing software without properly importing the data may result in undesired automatic formatting changes. These may impact identifier numbers and well numbers. If using the csv formatted file, please import correctly, otherwise use the provided software specific files which will maintain formatting.

procstep.procdesc: Step 1: Compiling data from each state. This was done by visiting state websites and downloading available relevant data or by direct data requests via email or phone call.

Step 2: Formatting the collected data into a standard format. State data were put into a standard national dataset format that included API number (or other identifying number), state, county, well name and number, well type and status, location coordinates, additional notes, and surface and subsurface land ownership. State specific notes are included below.
Alabama: Searched well data filtered by the term AB (abandoned) and downloaded results (Alabama Oil and Gas Board, 2025). Well status definitions from Geological Survey of Alabama website hosting State Oil and Gas Board of Alabama Administrative Code (2021) pdf.
Alaska: Downloaded "Official AOGCC Alaska Orphan Well List" from Alaska Oil and Gas Compact Commission (2024).
Arkansas: Downloaded shapefile from Arkansas Oil and Gas Commission (2025). Converted shapefile attribute table into excel spreadsheet. Filtered spreadsheet by well status "Abandoned Orphan".
California: Appendix 5 data on deserted and probably deserted wells from the Idle Wells Report, (California Geologic Energy Management Division, 2025) was merged with declared orphans from appendix 6 (also California Geologic Energy Management Division, 2025), and the data table from an "All Wells" shapefile (California Department of Conservation, 2025) using API numbers to make the join in database software. Daily updated "All Wells" data table provided the coordinates needed to be appended to the appendix 5 and 6 records.
Colorado: Due to problems isolating unplugged orphan wells from online data, a request was made by email to Colorado Oil and Gas Conservation Commission (2025). A spreadsheet file was sent to the authors with a list of unplugged orphaned wells in Colorado.
Illinois: Submitted a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) data request to staff at the Illinois Department of Natural Resources. Received data file from Illinois Department of Natural Resources (2025).
Indiana: Filtered well information from Indiana Department of Natural Resources (2025) by "orphan", "revoked", and "other orphan" and downloaded results. Definitions from IN DNR Orphaned & Abandoned Well Program webpage (2022). Data included no API numbers or coordinates, only public land survey system (PLSS) information and Indiana Geological Survey (IGS) identification numbers.
Kansas: Extracted wells from table in the Abandoned Oil and Gas Well Status Report (Kansas Corportation Commission, 2026) PDF table. Used Kansas Geological Survey Leoweb tool (KGS, 2026) to convert public land survey system (PLSS) locations to NAD83 coordinates. Added generic USGSID:KS#### sorting by county, then lease, then well number.
Kentucky: Downloaded Orphan Well List from Kentucky Energy and Environment Cabinet (2025) website. Carter coordinates (specific coordinate system used in Kentucky) was converted to NAD83 coordinates by USGS staff. XX wells missing API numbers were provided with a unique USGS ID.
Louisiana: Filtered well results on Louisiana SONRIS Data Portal on LA DNR (Louisiana Department of Natural Resources, 2025) website by well status “ACT 404 ORPHAN WELL-ENG" and “ACT 404 ORPHAN WELL-INJ", downloaded CSV results. Well status definitions from LA DNR (2022) website.
Michigan: Filtered well search status by "orphan" on Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (MI DEGLE) (2025) website’s Oil, Gas, & Minerals Division Data Explorer, and downloaded results.
Mississippi: Filtered by the terms “O” (orphaned) and “PO” (potentially orphaned) well status on Mississippi State Oil and Gas Board (2025) website and downloaded excel files results.
Missouri: Downloaded CSV of all oil and gas wells from Missouri Department of Natural Resources (2025) website. Filtered spreadsheet by "orphan", "abandoned", "abandoned no evidence", "abandoned known location", and "abandoned unknown location" well statuses and combined resulting data.
Montana: In the Orphan Wells tab on the Montana Bureau of Oil and Gas Conservation (2025) website, queried using inputs for Well type, equal to, oil OR gas. Downloaded data.
Nebraska: Downloaded "Nebraska Wells GIS Shapefile" from the Nebraska Oil and Gas Conservation Commission (NE OGCC) (2025) website. Converted shapefile attribute table to excel spreadsheet, filtered excel spreadsheet by "AB" (abandoned) to obtain orphan wells, as directed in email from NEOGCC staff.
Nevada: Downloaded excel spreadsheet from Nevada Division of Minerals Open Data Site (2025) Oil and Gas Well Search page. Filtered spreadsheet by "AB" (abandoned) well status.
New Mexico: Downloaded inactive wells spreadsheet from New Mexico Oil Conservation Division (2026a). Filtered 15 months of inactivity, the same filter that the state used to report potential orphan wells. Obtained coordinates by join with "New Mexico OCD Oil and Gas Wells" list from New Mexico Oil Conservation Division (2026b).
New York: Downloaded well data from New York Department of Environmental Conservation (2025) Oil & Gas Wells Data Search website. Filtered search by well status = “Unknown”, “Unknown Located”, and “Unknown Not Located”. Downloaded spreadsheets and merged.
North Dakota: Downloaded "OGD_Wells" shapefile from North Dakota Department of Mineral Resources (2025) Oil and Gas ArcIMS Viewer webpage. Converted shapefile attribute table into excel spreadsheet, filtered by "abandoned" well status. Abandoned well status definition from ND Oil & Gas Division.
Ohio: Attempts to filter publicly available data at https://gis.ohiodnr.gov/arcgis/rest/services/DOG_Services/Oilgas_Wells_public/MapServer/2 did not yield intended results. Upon request, Ohio Department of Natural Resources (2026) staff provided the requested data to the authors.
Oklahoma: Downloaded "Orphan Well List" spreadsheet from Oklahoma Conservation Commission (2025) Oil and Gas Conservation Division website.
Pennsylvania: Downloaded orphan well data from Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (2026). Filtered by "DEP orphan" and "DEP abandoned".
Tennessee: Received "forfeited" well data from Tennessee Department of Energy and Conservation (2025) staff. Converted NAD27 to NAD83 coordinates.
Texas: Downloaded spreadsheet of "Orphan Wells with Delinquent P-5 Greater Than 12 Months" data from Railroad Commission of Texas (2025) website.
Utah: Downloaded “Utah Oil and Gas Well Locations” file from Utah Division of Oil, Gas, and Mining (2025). Filtered operator by "Orphan-No Responsible Operator", and well status NOT = pa.
West Virginia: Data downloaded from the West Virginia Department of Environmental Protection (2025) Oil & Gas Wells website filtered by well status “Abandoned” and operator “Operator Unknown” and “Unknown”.
Wyoming: Filtered well class by any term including "orphaned" on Wyoming Oil & Gas Conservation Commission (2025) Orphan Well webpage. Downloaded data and filtered out "Subsequent Report of Abandonment" and "Permanently Abandoned" in Well Status column.

procstep.procdesc: Step 3: Data compilation. All state specific data were compiled into a national dataset.

Step 4: Quality control check on the preliminary dataset. General location checks, data formatting, value range checks, and other quality assurance and control checks were performed. Inconsequential data variation from source to source, such as capitalization, numerical digits reported, and well name / well number separation, were not reformatted in order to keep the data in a state as close as possible to that of the original source. Locations without coordinates were removed. Records with significant location errors, such as plotting in the wrong state far from borders were removed. Often these records had many wells at the same location, further indicating the record was incorrect.

Step 5: Surface landowner data added. Using Bureau of Land Management's (2026a) National SMA Surface Management Agency Area Polygons, a spatial join was performed to estimate the surface owner for each well location. If a federal agency is the estimated owner, both the department and agency were added to the dataset.

Step 6: Subsurface landowner data added. Available data was incomplete. Colorado, New Mexico, and Utah provided the subsurface owner (also called mineral rights owner) data with their orphan wells. Bureau of Land Management has published maps of federal ownership alone, for some states. Using Bureau of Land Management's data (2023, 2024a, 2024b, 2025b, and 2026a), a spatial join was performed to estimate the type of federal mineral rights for each well location. Examples of these federal rights include all mineral rights, just oil, or just coal etc. Because the subsurface owner and federal mineral rights data are estimates and come from different sources (the states and BLM respectively), there are some wells where the data from state and federal sources are not in agreement.
